newsitem.title: UK: UK's Ofgas approves sale of storage gas at NBP.
newsitem.headline: UK's Ofgas approves sale of storage gas at NBP.

text.p: U.K. gas industry regulator Ofgas has given the go-ahead to allow pipeline and storage operator Transco to sell surplus storage gas at the National Balancing Point (NBP) as well as within storage facilities.
Transco announced in June it was to sell around 180 million therms of gas held in storage by tender, with the transfer of ownership to take place in two storage facilities, Partington and Rough.

But shipper and generator Enron Corp submitted a proposed modification to the Network Code, the rulebook governing trade on the pipeline system, calling for the sale to take place at the National Balancing Point - in effect, on the spot market - as well as in storage.
Ofgas has now accepted this, and further proposed that the sale take place over two months instead of all on July 1 as originally scheduled under the Network Code.

Ofgas said on Tuesday it has accepted Enron's modification 157 and is proposing to amend the code "to enable Transco to issue a tender to sell off residual surplus gas in store and at the NBP over a period of two months." The date has yet to be fixed, but Ofgas is suggesting August and September.

August and September gas prices on the U.K. spot market softened on Tuesday afternoon as the industry anticipated the decision, which will result in extra gas for sale during the summer period when demand is at its lowest.
